claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch without disclosing the known weakness affecting the insurance claims triage segment, based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a non-core materiality characterization.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume may inform prioritization but do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Public governance principles can contextualize process quality but cannot replace missing policy predicates or approvals.
evidence_requests: Approved risk-acceptance record explicitly covering this named launch use case and authorizing launch without disclosure.
Admissible evidence that the insurance claims triage segment gap was remediated to target before certification.
Final legal review outcome addressing whether disclosure is required for the named pilot commitments.
Any executed customer-commitment interpretation or exception showing the segment is not in scope of the named launch use case.
specific_concerns: Available admissible evidence shows the missed target affects a named launch use case in two carrier pilot commitments, which meets the policy's materiality trigger.
The policy text states that non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
No admissible evidence shows the performance gap was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering nondisclosure.
Open legal review leaves a required policy predicate unresolved at the time of certification.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents do not answer the narrower disclosure requirement for a material limitation.
unsupported_claims: That certification without disclosure is policy-compliant on the present record.
That the non-core 8% traffic characterization is sufficient to negate materiality.
That public governance guidance on monitoring and model-card content substitutes for the policy-required resolution, disclosure, or approved risk acceptance.
